content: Dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA), when used as an herbal supplement, has been shown to interact with various medications by influencing the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. This interaction can lead to either an increase or decrease in the levels and effects of these drugs, necessitating careful monitoring or adjustment of therapy. Below are the specific interactions and their clinical implications: 1. DHEA and Dihydroergotamine (oral or intranasal): DHEA increases the levels or effects of dihydroergotamine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. It is recommended to avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 2. DHEA and Dronedarone: DHEA increases the levels or effects of dronedarone via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or consider an alternative therapy. 3. DHEA and Ergotamine: DHEA increases the levels or effects of ergotamine through CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 4. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 5. DHEA and Everolimus: DHEA increases the levels or effects of everolimus via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 6.
